records.theme: planned Crown rent from Essex Clandeboye colony
records.explanation: £5k annual rent was projected by Essex, not realised colonial profit. Do not add to actual cash.

records.theme: Queen loan to Essex Ulster scheme
records.explanation: Loan guaranteed by Essex estate, cannot count as Crown income or plunder.

records.theme: royal outlay proposed for six Ulster garrisons next two years
records.explanation: Projected expense c40k, do not add to actual royal spending.

records.theme: Essex colonisation Crown expenditure retrospectively estimated
records.explanation: DIB c80k Crown spent, uncertain exact period/overlap with other campaign accounts.

records.theme: Essex colonial venture personal losses
records.explanation: DIB c35k spent, venture failed and Essex sold lands; is COST not profit.

records.theme: Drake Anglo-French private raid Panama mule-train bullion seized
records.explanation: Library of Congress historical essay says ~£20k gold/silver, a retrospective gross prize estimate; no verified survivor shares, ship expenses, King/Queen remittance.

records.theme: Essex seized Brian O'Neill cattle then Piers aided recovering
records.explanation: DIB reports 10,000 head seized and then recovered with Piers help; do NOT count as English net extracted cattle.

records.theme: Essex massacre near Belfast following banquet
records.explanation: About 200 women, children and followers, not a financial profit metric.

records.theme: Rathlin castle defenders killed
records.explanation: Part of one massacre 1575, never add to later alternative total c600.

records.theme: Rathlin noncombatant refugees killed
records.explanation: 300–400 noncombatants in caves, largely women children; 200 defenders + 300–400 equals approximate 500–600 with uncertainties.

records.theme: Rathlin alternative academic biography rounded total
records.explanation: Same Rathlin killing as F09/F10; DIB Norreys c600 not additional 600. No audited named-person registry.

records.theme: Elizabeth I investment in Cathay Company Frobisher ore voyage
records.explanation: Queen contributed 1000 pounds; no proof of positive realized mining profits.

records.theme: Frobisher 1576–78 ore removed across voyages
records.explanation: Parks Canada calls the ~1,400 tons of extracted ore worthless; no independently audited mineral assay or profit, thus exact gold yield remains null.

records.theme: Frobisher kidnapped Inuit man
records.explanation: Person cannot be priced as chattel; voyage 1576 from Canadian Bay; source biog.

records.theme: Frobisher kidnapped Inuit Arnaq, Nutaaq, Kalicho
records.explanation: British Museum and Canada DCB; not a documented slave sale or sold human beings.

records.theme: Cacafuego captured 1 March 1579
records.explanation: Rich prize clearly captured but original manifest, metal weights, English cash distribution require documentary review; 1580 homecoming cannot be brought back to 1579. Period English captain account also gives 26 'tons' silver, 80 'pounds' gold and 13 chests reals: UNVERIFIED English narrative weights, cannot silently convert to tonnes/GBP or count separately from the same Cacafuego prize.

period_voyage_narrator_report.source_attribution: Francis Pretty voyage narrative surviving in Fordham University historical sourcebook
period_voyage_narrator_report.ship_taken: Nuestra Señora de la Concepción aka Cacafuego
period_voyage_narrator_report.historical_quoted_location: Cape de San Francisco (about 150 leagues south of Panama)

records.theme: Desmond Rebellion Munster 1579–83 later war death/depopulation
records.explanation: Severe depopulation evidenced across 1579–83, not attributed wholly to first six months of uprising.

records.theme: Mullaghmast O'More followers slain under promised protection; earliest individual number
records.explanation: Dowling mentions named victim and forty followers. Not a full researched death roll, and no justification to add to broad modern 100–400 estimates without nonoverlap.

records.theme: William Drury beheaded local Munster chiefs and commoners around Limerick
records.explanation: AFM M1576.15 independently records decapitations but no audited names/count/precise streets.

records.theme: Drury coerces Dal Cais homage/tax and enforces with troops after Ennis court
records.explanation: Tax/taking of submission described in AFM M1577.16; no tax receipts linked to event, do not invent alleged yearly profit.

records.theme: Nicholas Malby 1579 sack and plunder of Askeaton Franciscan friary
records.explanation: Irish government OPW confirms 1579 plunder; OPW separately confirms adjoining Askeaton Castle held out against Malby. No documented confiscated value nor verified 1579 victim count.

records.theme: 1579 Crown troop depredations in Munster despite safe-conduct/pledge to Desmond
records.explanation: Gaelic annal M1579.11 attests damaged fields/cattle/corn and royal broken promise, no quantified land/treasure/dues; destroyers also included other warfare sides, separate perpetrators.

records.theme: Henry Sidney 1576 local Loughrea conquest, seized hostages and prolonged garrison
records.explanation: AFM M1576.13 and retrospective M1580.26 support site garrison; NOT value of entire Clanrickard estates as UK cash.

records.theme: Henry Sidney compulsory replacement of arbitrary military cess with composition cash dues in Irish Pale
records.explanation: DIB scholarly account: Sidney sought to commute military cess exactions into cash composition; local gentry resisted and governors' actions were challenged. No historical estate list, levy figure, realized Crown revenue or complete land territorial acquisition can be inferred.

records.theme: Cathay Company commissioned Cornelius Ketel to paint two portraits of first captured Inuit man
records.explanation: Cambridge University Press Alden Vaughan paraphrases Cathay Company ledgers, 2 paintings at £5 each. Financial spending associated with display of captive person; not sale price, not Crown receipts or profit.

records.theme: Kalicho and Arnaq captured in Baffin Island and buried in Bristol 1577 parish St Stephen
records.explanation: Same two adults already counted in C9-F15 captive trio. Captivity and death documented; this adds exact parish placement and dates, not two additional victims.

records.theme: Queen Elizabeth received profits from 1577 faculties commission, manuscript amount not transcribed
records.historical_document: Cotton MS Titus B XIII/1 ff 270r–270v
records.explanation: British Library manuscript catalogue names profit accruing to Queen via English/Irish church faculties commission in 1577. The accounts are not read; not possible to assign any exact Crown receipt nor classify as violence profit without identifying payers/collection.

records.theme: Royal Irish field army supply cost estimates 14 June1578 per Sidney MS document
records.original_manuscript: Cotton MS Titus B X/1 ff157v–161r
records.explanation: BL original catalogue proves estimate of victuals attached to 14 June1578 letter. Without figures and paid vouchers, no cash total or assumed quantities of seized peasant crops.

do_not_sum: 1575 Rathlin 200 defenders and 300–400 civilians and alternative total 600 overlap
£5k proposed yearly rent not income, £10k royal loan not revenue and £40k fort budget proposal not spend
£80k actual royal cost and £35k Essex cost not colony fiscal return
£20k privately seized Spain bullion cannot equal Crown net
Frobisher £1000 royal investment not profitable ore gain; 1400t worthless ore not realized gold
1579 prize would be distributed after return 1580 not recognized in 1579 English Exchequer

Francis Pretty's 26 tons silver, 80 lb gold, 13 chests reales are not independent events or certified customs ledger; treat as a single narrator's Cacafuego prize narrative, no automatic gold equivalent or sterling conversion
Mullaghmast 40 followers named in one source are NOT another 40 to add to every other modern victim estimate; incident date contested 1577 vs reconstructed March1578
C9-F26 named Kalicho and Arnaq Bristol burial records are the SAME adult victims in C9-F15, not additional 2 Inuit taken.
Cathay Company £5 each portrait costs are expenditures for exploitation/displays of captive Inuit, not received income nor human monetary valuation.
1577 Crown commission for faculties archive ledger and 1578 army victualling estimate identified only by shelfmarks, amounts unread. Do not invent or classify automatically as income from massacres.
